recipes.name: Whiskey Hamburgers
ingredients_raw: 1 (1.5 fluid ounce) jigger whiskey (such as Jack Daniel's®)

steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat; lightly oil the grate.
Combine ground beef, beer, Worcestershire sauce, whiskey, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper in a large bowl; mix until evenly combined. Shape mixture into 6 patties.

Cook on the preheated grill until meat is cooked to your desired degree of doneness, 5 to 8 minutes per side for well done. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Whiskey Hamburgers
raw_recipe.description: These whiskey burgers are made with beer, a splash of Jack Daniels whiskey, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, and onion for a unique flavor profile.

review.reviewBody: Great hamburger! I love cooking with beer, but never thought to add whiskey before. I scaled this down to 4 servings for 1 pound of ground beef. I used minced garlic from a jar instead of garlic powder and instead of Sam Adam's used Michelob Ultra. I think any type of full bodied beer will work fine in this recipe. After mixing the ground beef, we let it set for a half hour in the fridge before making the patties to let the flavors come together. These burgers came out very moist and juicy. We will definitely make these again. They were perfect on a toasted roll with melted cheese, lettuce, tomato and onion.

I substitute 12 ounces of Impossible burger, minced garlic and finely chopped red onion, for 4 burgers. It’s our favorite burger (2 meat eaters and 2 vegetarians). I sauté sliced mushrooms, adding Worcestershire sauce and bourbon after the mushrooms are browned and cooking till the liquid mostly evaporates. Those go on top. Yum!

A delicious burger, and the taste was even improved as they were cooked on a charcoal grill rather than a gas grill. I used organic 85/15 beef and these burgers did not shrink up, at all! I mixed them up early in the day so that the flavors had time to meld. Once I took them out of the fridge, I let rest about 30 minutes to take off the chill. We added cheese, lettuce, pickles and tomatoes and enjoyed 'Honey Mustard Macaroni Salad' from AR and fresh veggies along with the burgers.

the burgers came out okay but i was expecting something more.. i subbed 4 cloves of garlic for the garlic powder and 1/2 a yellow onion for the onion powder.. i could taste the beer (budlite) and the whiskey (bushmills) in the burgers but i wanted a punchy component.. we cooked these in the oven as it was raining outside.. on a positive note, the burgers were very moist and juicy

Made this with some Killian's and Grant's Scotch whiskey. We also used diced fresh onion instead of powder which adds a nice little crunch. My wife said it is the best homemade burger she's ever had and that it rivals most nice restaurant burgers. I have no complaints, I just gave it 4 of 5 because it was really good and juicy, but there wasn't anything over the top, just a really great burger recipe. I made 1/4 lb patties about 3/8-1/2" thick and cooked them at about 350 for 7-9 minutes. The 7-8 minute mark seemed to be ideal. The last two that stayed on an extra minute or two were a little more dry, but that goes for any burgers, not just these.

So Good!
I had to alter a bit since I had pre-formed hamburger patties (left over from a huge party). 

Rather than adding to the hamburger then forming the patties, I simply marinated them for 60 minutes then brushed more 'sauce' on during the cooking

The only change to ingrediants I made was to use minced garlic rather than powdered, I also used a seasoning blend that I make during the grilling.
Followed recipe and added 1c diced onion and 1 diced jalapeño . They were moist and had a great flavor! A real keeper recipe.
Town Branch Bourbon worked out well for this recipe, topped with eggs on Auntie Millie Pretzel bun, would also suggest a nice Cider as a pairing for this yummy dish.

I tried this on turkey burgers with lots of cayenne (because my baby likes things extra spicy). It was delicious! I did add a little extra whiskey right before they finished cooking, so there was kind of a whiskey glaze. Thanks so much for the recipe:)

These are amazing! I noticed a lot of people turned off by the strong whiskey flavor, so I only used half of the whiskey and replaced the rest with beer. I used very lean beef and tossed an egg in to keep it all together. This is now my go-to burger recipe.

GREAT !!! with a FEW Changes ..i skipped all the powdered stuff, added frsh minced garlic and std diced vidalia onions, some crispy crumbled bacon and blue cheese crumbles...turned out delicious !!! def in my list to make again !
So good!! Loved this. The burgers were so juicy and flavorful!

Who thought to add Whiskey to a hamburger! I adjusted the recipe to add Stone Ground Horseradish Mustard (or one of your choice). I like my steaks/hamburgers Medium-Rare so totally changed the cooking Time-loved the result
This was so bad, I couldn’t eat it
These were a huge hit for my BBQ, I will definitely make them again!
Amazing, that’s all I can say
These were very tasty! I will definitely make this again. A nice change from a plain run of the mill burger
This is a delicious recipe! I used chopped onions and chopped garlic instead of the powders. I’m keeping this recipe for sure! Thanks for sharing!
Delicious, juicy and lots of flavor! Made it yesterday with my sister for a family gathering and it was a HUGE success! Will definitely mark this recipe as a favorite.
way to moist. could not get a good seat on the burgers. tasted just ok.
